## Purpose
Defines `WorkflowRun`, the SQLAlchemy model for a single pipeline execution — the durable row that tracks a run's status, input/output, per-agent outputs, token usage, and the growing set of run-scoped fields (ownership, selections, OpenDesign context) added additively across many migrations.

## Shape
- `WorkflowRun` — the single class/table (`workflow_runs`), with `id` as the canonical run identifier used end-to-end by the engine, state machine, and artifact store (`pipeline_run_id` was dropped in migration 0013).
- Core lifecycle columns — `status`, `type`, `input`/`output`, `agent_outputs`, `agent_count`, `duration`, `error`, `token_usage`, timestamps.
- Phase-additive columns grouped by migration — Phase 3 (`parent_run_id`, `execution_gate`, `execution_strategy`), Phase 5 authz (`owner_id`, `workspace_id`, `plan_id`, `budget_snapshot_json`), Phase 22 (`deliverable_mimetype`/`deliverable_filename`), WR-02 (`selections_json`), KAN-120 (`od_context_json`).
- Relationships — `user`, self-referential `parent_run`, and `clarifications` (lazy dynamic); the legacy `artifacts` relationship was removed when the thin `workflow_artifacts` table was dropped in favor of `artifact_refs`.

## Why this shape
Each new field is nullable and added additively by its own migration specifically to preserve byte/event parity for legacy rows (INV-3, called out repeatedly in the inline comments) — new capabilities are backfilled or default to a no-op rather than requiring a backfill migration that could change existing run behavior.
